newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Denmark says Albania's Berisha should stand down.
newsitem.headline: Denmark says Albania's Berisha should stand down.

text.p: Danish Foreign Minister Niels Helveg Petersen said on Saturday Albanian President Sali Berisha should stand down to help end the crisis which has erupted in the Balkan country.

"I'm sure that if President Berisha were to step down that would in some ways improve the situation in Albania," he told reporters at the start of an informal meeting of EU foreign ministers in the Dutch country town of Apeldoorn.

Petersen, whose country currently holds the rotating chairmanship of the 54-member Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), said he personally backed the sending of a foreign intervention force to Albania, but he forecast disagreements at the EU meeting over how to respond to the crisis.

"I'm in favour of the international community sending in some kind of force, with a manadate to be defined," he said, but added that he expected "solid disagreement" among the 15 EU countries on options for responding to the crisis.
The crisis in Albania and the country's call for help looked set to capture the agenda on Saturday at the EU meeting.
OSCE mediator Franz Vranitzky, a former Austrian chancellor who is reporting to Petersen, said on Friday that there was no alternative to foreign intervention to halt Albania's descent into chaos.
Officials said the EU ministers were likely to throw their support behind the mediation efforts of the OSCE.
